You are building a differential-test corpus for a byte-exact JavaScript reimplementation of this Python program:

    import yaml, argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(yaml.dump(yaml.safe_load(args.a), default_style='|'))

Your assigned category is "scalars-plain":
Plain (unquoted) scalars: every YAML 1.1 implicit-resolution edge case — ints (decimal, octal 0o and 0NN, hex, binary, sexagesimal like 1:30, underscores), floats (leading dot, trailing dot, exponents with and without explicit sign, sexagesimal floats, .inf/.nan in all casings), bools (yes/no/on/off/true/false/y/n in every casing), nulls (~, null, Null, NULL, empty), strings that ALMOST look like numbers (08, 1e, 1.2.3, +.5, _1, 1:60, 0X1F), and the special "=" value token.

TASK: write a Node ESM script at /workspace/probe/corpus/gen_scalars-plain.mjs that writes AT LEAST 60 distinct test-case files into /workspace/probe/corpus/scalars-plain/ named 001.txt, 002.txt, ... Each file's ENTIRE byte content is one value for the --a argument (a YAML document, possibly multi-line, possibly with a trailing newline).

Rules:
- Use only: import { writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
- Build the cases as a plain JS array of strings, then write them out. Use \n, \t, \u.... escapes in the JS source rather than literal control characters.
- Cases must be DISTINCT from one another and must actually exercise your category. Prefer many small focused cases over a few large ones. Include obvious/common forms as well as pathological ones.
- Do NOT include a case whose text starts with "-" unless it also contains a space before any newline (argparse would swallow it as an option flag). Concretely: if the string starts with "-", make sure the FIRST line contains a space, e.g. "- a" is fine, "---" alone is not.
- Some cases SHOULD be invalid YAML if your category calls for it; that is expected and useful.
- Avoid the NUL character.

Then RUN your script with: cd /workspace/probe/corpus && node gen_scalars-plain.mjs
Then sanity-check that the files exist and a few of them produce sensible behaviour from the reference binary, e.g.:
    /workspace/dataset/test14_executable --a "$(cat /workspace/probe/corpus/scalars-plain/001.txt)"
(that shell form mangles trailing newlines, it is only a smoke test).

Do not modify anything outside /workspace/probe/corpus/. Do not read or write /output.

Return ONLY a one-line summary: the category key and the number of case files written.

import { writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';

// Category: scalars-plain
// Plain (unquoted) scalars and YAML 1.1 implicit resolution edge cases.
// NOTE: PyYAML's 1.1 resolver quirks exercised here:
//   - exponents require an explicit sign: 5.67e-8 is a float, 1.23e10 is a string
//   - 0o17 / 0X1F / 0B101 are NOT numbers (only 0NN octal, 0x hex, 0b binary)
//   - single-letter y / n are NOT bools in PyYAML
//   - sexagesimal ints need a leading [1-9]; sexagesimal floats allow a leading 0
//   - ".Nan" is a string but ".NaN" is a float
//   - "=" resolves to tag:yaml.org,2002:value -> constructor error as a value,
//     silently turned into a str as a mapping key
// Rule: no case may start with "-" unless its first line also contains a space,
// so every negative form is wrapped in a mapping/flow context.

const cases = [
  // ---- nulls -------------------------------------------------------------
  '~',
  'null',
  'Null',
  'NULL',
  'nULL',
  'NuLl',
  'none',
  'None',
  'NONE',
  '',
  'k:',
  'k: ~',
  'k: null',
  '~: 1',
  'a: null\nb: ~\nc:\nd: NULL',
  '[~, null, Null, NULL, ]',

  // ---- bools -------------------------------------------------------------
  'yes',
  'Yes',
  'YES',
  'yEs',
  'no',
  'No',
  'NO',
  'nO',
  'true',
  'True',
  'TRUE',
  'tRue',
  'false',
  'False',
  'FALSE',
  'fALSE',
  'on',
  'On',
  'ON',
  'oN',
  'off',
  'Off',
  'OFF',
  'oFf',
  'y',
  'Y',
  'n',
  'N',
  'yes: no\ntrue: false\non: off',
  '[y, Y, n, N, yes, Yes, YES]',
  '{on: off, ON: OFF, On: Off}',

  // ---- ints: decimal + underscores ---------------------------------------
  '0',
  '+0',
  'k: -0',
  '1',
  '123',
  '+123',
  'k: -123',
  '1_000',
  '1_000_000',
  '+1_0',
  '1_',
  '_1',
  '1__2',
  '0_',
  '1_2_3_4_5',

  // ---- ints: octal / hex / binary ----------------------------------------
  '00',
  '007',
  '017',
  '0644',
  'k: -017',
  '0_17',
  '08',
  '09',
  '0o17',
  '0o777',
  '0x1f',
  '0x1F',
  '0X1F',
  '0xdeadBEEF',
  '0x_1f',
  '0x',
  '0xg',
  '0b101',
  '0B101',
  '0b102',
  '0b_1_0_1',
  '0b',
  'a: 08\nb: 8\nc: 0o10\nd: 010',
  '[0o17, 017, 0x1f, 0X1F, 0b101, 0B101]',

  // ---- ints: sexagesimal -------------------------------------------------
  '1:30',
  '12:34:56',
  '190:20:30',
  '1:60',
  '0:30',
  'k: -1:30',
  '+1:30',
  '1:3',
  '1:03',
  '3:',
  'k: :3',
  '1:2:3:4',
  '1_0:30',

  // ---- floats ------------------------------------------------------------
  '1.0',
  'k: -1.0',
  '+1.0',
  '.5',
  'k: -.5',
  '+.5',
  '0.',
  '1.',
  'k: -1.',
  '.0',
  '1.2.3',
  '0.0.0',
  '1_0.5_5',
  '.5_0',
  '.',
  '..',

  // ---- floats: exponents (PyYAML 1.1 needs an explicit sign) -------------
  '1.23e10',
  '5.67e-8',
  '5.67e+8',
  '1.0E-3',
  '1.0E+3',
  '1e5',
  '1e',

  '.5e+3',
  '.5e3',
  '1e+',
  '.e+5',
  'large: 1.23e10\nsmall: 5.67e-8',

  // ---- floats: inf / nan casings -----------------------------------------
  '.inf',
  '.Inf',
  '.INF',
  '.iNf',
  'k: -.inf',
  '+.inf',
  'k: -.Inf',
  'inf',
  'Inf',
  'Infinity',
  '.nan',
  '.NaN',
  '.NAN',
  '.Nan',
  'k: -.nan',
  'nan',
  'NaN',
  '[.inf, .INF, .nan, .NAN]',

  // ---- floats: sexagesimal -----------------------------------------------
  '1:30.5',
  '0:30.5',
  '1:30.',
  '190:20:30.15',
  'k: -1:30.5',

  // ---- the "=" value token -----------------------------------------------
  '=',
  'k: =',
  '=: 1',
  '==',
  '[=]',
  'a: 1\n=: 2',
  '{=: =}',

  // ---- strings that almost look like numbers -----------------------------
  '1,000',
  '1 000',
  '1-2',
  '1+2',
  '++1',
  '1.0.0.0',
  '1st',
  '2e2e2',
  '0.0e0',
  'k: --1',

  // ---- comments, whitespace and multi-line plain folding -----------------
  '#1',
  '1#c',
  '1 #c',
  'true#x',
  'null #x',
  ' yes',
  'yes ',
  '   17   ',
  'yes\n',
  '0x1f\n',
  '1\n2',
  'yes\nno',
  '1.5\n  2.5',
  'k: 1\n  2',
  '\t1',

  // ---- plain scalars as keys / in collections ----------------------------
  '{1: a, 1.0: b, true: c, ~: d}',
  '? yes\n: no',
  '0x10: 16\n020: 16',
  'k: [1, 1.0, yes, null, 0o7]',
  '1.0: x',
  '.inf: x',

  // ---- invalid: characters that cannot start a plain scalar --------------
  '@yes',
  '`no`',
  'k: @1',
  'k: `1`',
  '%1',
];

const seen = new Set();
for (const c of cases) {
  if (seen.has(c)) throw new Error('duplicate case: ' + JSON.stringify(c));
  seen.add(c);
  if (c.startsWith('-') && !c.split('\n')[0].includes(' ')) {
    throw new Error('bad leading dash: ' + JSON.stringify(c));
  }
  if (c.includes('�')) throw new Error('NUL in case');
}

const dir = '/workspace/probe/corpus/scalars-plain';
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
cases.forEach((c, i) => {
  writeFileSync(`${dir}/${String(i + 1).padStart(3, '0')}.txt`, c);
});
console.log('scalars-plain: wrote', cases.length, 'cases to', dir);
